subject: Request: telemetry handback & SLA carveout for Arkline private VPC
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@arkline.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@arkline.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: telemetry handback & SLA carveout for Arkline private VPC

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Arkline is excited about the performance gains on Redwood Dedicated, and we're close to finalizing procurement. One open item from our security and networking teams: Arkline will be operating customer-facing edge routers and a private peering fabric for our users. We need explicit SLA carveout language for any latency or availability issues that are demonstrably caused by Arkline-managed network/edge components.

Specifically we need two things to satisfy procurement and our SOC reviewers:
- A short contract clause stating Redwood will not be held responsible for latency/outage attributable to customer-managed edge/peering components and a clear attribution process.
- A telemetry "handback" spec: an agreed mechanism and data set Redwood will consume (read-only feed or uploaded evidence) to validate incidents (examples: traceroutes, NetFlow summaries, router syslogs, and a sample of pcap/traces).

I've attached a one-page network diagram and we can share more if helpful. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a read-only Prometheus/Pushgateway feed for basic metrics, and what minimum evidence you need to disqualify an event from Redwood SLA credits?

Procurement would like this language and an evidence checklist before the order goes to legal — can we aim to have a proposal by end of week?

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of SRE, Arkline
arkline.ai

Attachment: arkline_network_arch.pdf (diagram, 1pg)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@arkline.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry handback & SLA carveout for Arkline private VPC

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. We're glad Arkline is progressing with Dedicated.

Short answers up-front:
- Yes, we can include a narrowly scoped carveout for latency/outages attributable to customer-managed edge/peering.
- Yes, we can accept a read-only metrics feed and a set of forensic artifacts for incident attribution.

Next steps I propose:
1) Sync call with your SRE + our infra/product/legal so we can align on acceptable evidence and timing (30 minutes).
2) Draft suggested clause and an "evidence checklist" for procurement to review.
3) Technical spec for telemetry handback (metrics types, retention window, sample rates, secure transfer).

To help legal and product scope the clause, could you confirm:
- Will Arkline be the primary owner of the BGP peering sessions and NAT for customer flows?
- Do you have an existing monitoring endpoint we can subscribe to (Prometheus remote_read / read-only Grafana API / S3 exports)?

I've looped in Kim (contracts) and Vivek (serving runtime) to help with proposed language and operational impacts. Are you available Thursday 6/22 at 9am PT?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry handback & SLA carveout for Arkline private VPC

Jonas — thanks for taking point. Drafted below is an initial carveout + evidence spec we can offer to Arkline for procurement review. I kept the language narrowly scoped to avoid broad liability gaps. Please review and flag any runtime implications.

Proposed contract paragraph (draft):
"Redwood Inference's uptime and latency commitments exclude degradation or interruption of Service to the extent directly caused by Customer-controlled network infrastructure, including but not limited to Customer-operated edge routers, private peering links, and Network Address Translation (NAT) devices ("Customer Network Components"). For an incident to be excluded from Redwood's SLA calculation, Customer must provide timely and reasonable evidence demonstrating causation as described in the Attribution and Evidence Procedure. Redwood will evaluate such evidence in good faith and may engage mutually agreed third-party network forensics if necessary.

Attribution and Evidence Procedure (summary):
- Minimum data required from Customer: traceroute outputs covering affected paths (pre- and post-aggregation), NetFlow/ sFlow summaries for the incident window, router syslog excerpts with timestamps, sample packet captures (pcap) limited to metadata where required, and configuration diffs if a config change is suspected.
- Telemetry handback options: (A) read-only access to a metrics endpoint (Prometheus remote_read or read-only Grafana API) with at least 1m scrape cadence for relevant metrics; (B) S3 bucket with hourly metric exports and a signed manifest; (C) secure upload of forensic artifacts via SFTP/Secure API.
- Timing: Customer must submit evidence within 72 hours of incident detection; Redwood will acknowledge within 24 hours and provide an attribution determination within 7 calendar days from receipt of complete evidence.

Operational notes (for internal SRE/product):
- We should support Prometheus remote_read subscription and S3 ingest for metric exports.
- Forpcap ingestion we will accept metadata-only samples unless both parties approve deeper packet inspection under an MSA addendum.

Attachments: I created a short template (sla_carveout_template.docx) that maps the clause to specific evidence fields for procurement.

If this looks OK I can send to Emily and propose the Thu slot. Vivek — please call out any constraints on evidence processing (rate, retention, costs). Grace — will need your sign-off on the timing commitments to customers.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@arkline.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@arkline.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry handback & SLA carveout for Arkline private VPC

Jonas / Kim / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft language. Arkline is aligned with the narrow carveout and the 72-hour evidence window. A few confirmations and an ask:

- Arkline will be primary owner of the BGP sessions and NAT for the customer-facing edge (confirmed).
- We can provide a read-only Prometheus remote_read endpoint for the relevant peering/egress metrics (1m scrape cadence) and hourly S3 metric exports for the preceding 30 days.
- For packet captures we can provide redacted pcaps (metadata-only) and full pcaps under an NDA/forensics engagement; we prefer Redwood to accept metadata samples for routine attribution.

Procurement wants an explicit line about "mutually agreed third-party forensics" only being invoked if either party disputes attribution after the 7-day window. That's acceptable.

We're ready to move this into an amendment. I'll open a procurement ticket (ARK-4521) and push a DocuSign draft; please confirm who at Redwood should be the signing representative for this amendment. If possible, we'd like the amendment signed by next Wednesday 7/4 so our Q3 deployment can proceed.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of SRE, Arkline

Attachment: none
